data.best_text: May, June and September for life outdoors without the high-summer heat, December for the Christmas markets.
data.day_budget_note: Per person per day excluding flights: a share of a mid-range double room, food, local transport and one sight. A rough estimate.

stay.label: Weekend
stay.text: The Reichstag dome, the Holocaust Memorial and the East Side Gallery.

stay.label: Long weekend
stay.text: Time for Bernauer Straße, Museum Island and an evening in Kreuzberg.

stay.label: One week
stay.text: Add Potsdam and quieter days in Prenzlauer Berg.

areas.name: Mitte
areas.text: Closest to the sights and the central station. The most expensive and least local.

areas.name: Prenzlauer Berg
areas.text: Quiet streets, cafés and a Sunday market. Tram and U-Bahn into the centre.

areas.name: Kreuzberg
areas.text: The most food and nightlife. Lively at night.

areas.name: Friedrichshain
areas.text: Cheaper, close to the East Side Gallery and the clubs.

areas.name: Around Kottbusser Tor and Görlitzer Park
areas.text: Good for eating, but rowdy at night. Stay a few blocks away.

transport.text: About 23 minutes to the central station via Südkreuz and Potsdamer Platz. Together with the RE20, up to five trains an hour.
One and the same ticket is valid on everything. A single ticket is valid for two hours in one direction.

events.name: Berlinale
events.text: The film festival. Tickets for the screenings are sold to the public.

events.name: Berlin Half Marathon
events.text: Streets in the centre are closed during the race.

events.name: Karneval der Kulturen
events.text: A street festival and parade in Kreuzberg. The dates are expected, not confirmed.

events.name: The Pergamon Museum reopens
events.text: The museum on Museum Island opens after the renovation.

events.name: Berlin Art Week
events.text: Exhibitions in galleries all over the city.

events.name: Berlin Marathon
events.text: One of the world's biggest races. Hotels are expensive that weekend and the centre is closed off.

seasons.name: Christmas markets
seasons.text: The first ones open on 23 November.

month_notes: Cold, grey and short days. Cheap to stay.
Spring is slow to arrive, but the days are getting longer.
The outdoor terraces open. The weather can turn.
Warm and green. The beer gardens are open.
Long bright evenings and plenty of life outdoors.
High summer. It can get hot, and many Berliners are away.
High summer and swimming lakes. Lots of tourists.
Warm but not hot, and fewer tourists.
Autumn. Cooler, with lovely colours in the parks.
Grey and cold before the Christmas markets open.
Christmas markets all over the city. Cold and dark early.

prices.summary: About the same as at home in restaurants, and cheaper for beer.
tips: A double room costs 160–220 euros per night on average according to Kayak, depending on which of Kayak's pages you read.

rows.note: According to Settle in Berlin, not Numbeo.

DE-fakta-inresa.title: Passport or national ID card
DE-fakta-inresa.summary: Bring a passport or national ID card. A driving licence does not count as a travel document.
DE-fakta-inresa.body: A national ID card is valid for travel within the EU and Schengen. A Swedish driving licence is not normally accepted as a travel document.

DE-fakta-mobil.title: Use data and call as at home
DE-fakta-mobil.summary: EU roaming: the same price as in Sweden.
DE-fakta-mobil.body: You pay as at home for calls, texts and data, but the operator may set a cap on data abroad.

DE-fakta-alkohol-16.title: Beer and wine from age 16
DE-fakta-alkohol-16.summary: Beer, wine and sparkling wine may be sold to anyone aged 16 or over.
DE-fakta-alkohol-16.body: The limit applies both in shops and where alcohol is served.

DE-fakta-alkohol-18.title: Spirits from age 18
DE-fakta-alkohol-18.summary: Spirits, liqueurs and alcopops require age 18.
DE-fakta-alkohol-18.body: This also applies to mixed drinks containing spirits.

DE-berlin-fakta-ta-sig-dit.title: BER to the central station in 23 minutes
DE-berlin-fakta-ta-sig-dit.summary: The FEX airport train runs via Südkreuz and Potsdamer Platz.
DE-berlin-fakta-ta-sig-dit.body: The station is directly below the terminal. It takes about 14 minutes to Südkreuz.

DE-berlin-fakta-abc-biljett.title: The airport requires an ABC ticket
DE-berlin-fakta-abc-biljett.summary: BER is in zone C. An ordinary AB ticket is not enough.
DE-berlin-fakta-abc-biljett.body: The ticket is valid on all transport within the zones, including the airport train. Buy an ABC ticket at the airport for the trip into the city.

DE-berlin-fakta-biljettpriser.title: Single ticket 4 euros, to the airport 5 euros
DE-berlin-fakta-biljettpriser.summary: AB costs 4 euros and ABC 5 euros. A 24-hour AB ticket costs 11.20 euros.
DE-berlin-fakta-biljettpriser.body: A 24-hour ABC ticket costs 12.90 euros. A small-group day ticket is valid for up to five people and costs 35.30 euros for AB. The prices apply in 2026 and will partly rise in January 2027.

DE-berlin-fakta-turistskatt.title: City tax of 7.5 per cent
DE-berlin-fakta-turistskatt.summary: The tax is 7.5% of the net room price. Breakfast is not included in the calculation.
DE-berlin-fakta-turistskatt.body: It applies to all paid overnight stays, since April 2024 including business trips. Check whether the tax is included in the price you see when you book.

DE-berlin-fakta-sondagsstangt.title: Shops are closed on Sundays
DE-berlin-fakta-sondagsstangt.summary: Almost all shops are closed on Sundays. Buy food on Saturday.
DE-berlin-fakta-sondagsstangt.body: The exceptions are shops at railway stations and airports. On eight Sundays a year, including some in Advent, shops may open 1–8 pm. Monday to Saturday they may open around the clock.

DE-berlin-reichstagskupolen.name: The Reichstag dome
DE-berlin-reichstagskupolen.summary: Free, but you must register in advance.
DE-berlin-reichstagskupolen.body: The dome and roof terrace cost nothing. Register via the Bundestag's form with name and date of birth. It is not possible to book by phone. A free audio guide is included.

DE-berlin-murmuseet-bernauer.name: The Berlin Wall Memorial
DE-berlin-murmuseet-bernauer.summary: Free. A section of the Wall still stands here with the border strip and a watchtower.
DE-berlin-murmuseet-bernauer.body: The memorial lies along Bernauer Straße, which was the border between East and West. The outdoor exhibition is open every day 8 am–10 pm. The documentation centre and visitor centre are open Tuesday–Sunday 10 am–6 pm.

DE-berlin-east-side-gallery.name: East Side Gallery
DE-berlin-east-side-gallery.summary: 1,316 metres of Wall with paintings along the Spree. Free and always open.
DE-berlin-east-side-gallery.body: This is the longest continuous section of the Wall still standing. It is in Friedrichshain and has been managed since 2018 by the Berlin Wall Foundation.

DE-berlin-museumsinsel.name: Museum Island
DE-berlin-museumsinsel.summary: Five museums on an island in the Spree. A World Heritage Site since 1999.
DE-berlin-museumsinsel.body: The Pergamon Museum is completely closed for renovation and reopens on 4 June 2027, then with the Pergamon Altar. Until then, the exhibition Pergamonmuseum. Das Panorama is shown opposite the island. The other museums are open.

DE-berlin-forintelsemonumentet.name: The Holocaust Memorial
DE-berlin-forintelsemonumentet.summary: 2,711 concrete blocks of different heights near the Brandenburg Gate. Always open.
DE-berlin-forintelsemonumentet.body: The field is free and can be entered from any side. Beneath it is an exhibition, Ort der Information, which is open Tuesday–Sunday 10 am–6 pm and is also free.

DE-berlin-tv-tornet.name: The TV Tower
DE-berlin-tv-tornet.summary: 368 metres high at Alexanderplatz. Book a time online.
DE-berlin-tv-tornet.body: With an online ticket you choose the day and time and skip the ticket queue. Tickets often sell out, so book in advance.

mat-currywurst.name: Currywurst
mat-currywurst.hint: Sliced sausage with ketchup and curry powder.

bakverk-brezel.name: Brezel
bakverk-brezel.hint: A salted pretzel made from lye bread.

bakverk-berliner.name: Jam doughnut
bakverk-berliner.hint: A fried bun filled with jam.

dryck-gluhwein.name: Glühwein at a Christmas market
dryck-gluhwein.hint: Hot spiced wine in a mug with a deposit.

sevardhet-ampelmann.name: Ampelmännchen
sevardhet-ampelmann.hint: The little man with a hat in the pedestrian crossing lights.

DE-berlin-ide-kupolen.title: Evening visit to the Reichstag dome
DE-berlin-ide-kupolen.body: Register before the trip and choose a time at dusk.

DE-berlin-ide-muren.title: Follow the Wall in a day
DE-berlin-ide-muren.body: Start at Bernauer Straße in the morning and take the S-Bahn to the East Side Gallery in the afternoon. Both are free.

DE-berlin-ide-gratis.title: A free day in the centre
DE-berlin-ide-gratis.body: The Reichstag dome, the Holocaust Memorial and the Brandenburg Gate are within walking distance of each other.

DE-berlin-ide-museumsinsel.title: A rainy day on Museum Island
DE-berlin-ide-museumsinsel.body: Choose one or two museums. The Pergamon Museum is closed until June 2027.

DE-present-julmarknadsmugg.name: Mulled-wine mug from a Christmas market
DE-present-julmarknadsmugg.body: Every market has its own mug for the year. You pay a deposit and get to keep it.

DE-present-choklad.name: German chocolate
DE-present-choklad.body: Square bars in many flavours that are not sold at home.

DE-present-ampelmann.name: Ampelmann souvenir
DE-present-ampelmann.body: The little man from the East German traffic lights is on everything from mugs to key rings.
